contract: POST /api/items/:id/cover rejects in this order: no token 401, unknown item 404 (before any permission check), no access to the item's library 403, no update permission 403, no upload permission 403, and no url and no cover file 400; every rejection writes no file, changes no row and emits no item_updated. POST cover with body.url downloads the image through fileUtils.downloadImageFile (content type image/*, not svg) to metadata/items/:id/cover.<ext>, validates the image signature, stores media.coverPath, answers {success:true,cover} with the stored path, moves updatedAt and emits item_updated to users with access to the item. POST cover with a multipart cover file requires a supported extension (png, jpg, jpeg, webp), stores metadata/items/:id/cover.<ext> with the uploaded bytes, removes older cover images of the same item whose extension is in that allowlist, keeps other files, purges the resized cover cache, sets media.coverPath, moves updatedAt and emits item_updated; repeating the same upload succeeds again. POST cover answers 400 and changes no row, file or event when the url serves a non-image content type, when the body is not a recognised image signature, or when the multipart extension is not in the allowlist; a multipart part named other than cover with no url is also 400.
exceptions: force is not applicable: the route has no force or override mode; a new cover simply replaces the old one.
Only loopback cover urls are used: the SSRF whitelist is set to 127.0.0.1 and literal private addresses are rejected without a network attempt.
